source.title: A Minimalist Dataset for Systematic Generalization of Perception, Syntax, and Semantics
source.authors: Qing Li; Siyuan Huang; Yining Hong; Yixin Zhu; Ying Wu; Song-Chun Zhu

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Its text identifies the publication as ICLR 2023.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports scaling of HINT test accuracy, not the held-out pretraining loss, compute-optimal allocation, or other outcomes named by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures accuracy as model size and training-set size vary, and gives accuracy-fit equations and a projection. These are not results on pretraining loss or the other outcomes specified in V1–V7, so the scaling results are recorded as findings that fit no version. Architecture comparisons and cited scaling-law results are not recorded as claim-version results.
record.test_reason: The study trains task-specific seq2seq models on the HINT arithmetic benchmark and fits log-linear trends of test accuracy against model size and training-set size. It cites Kaplan et al. and Henighan et al. only to motivate asking whether scaling would solve HINT. It measures no pretraining loss, no compute-optimal allocation, and no downstream accuracy of a pretrained language model as a function of scale or loss. Its accuracy-scaling result therefore fits no version and is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that the scaling trends of test accuracy with dataset and model size make it impractical to solve HINT by scaling alone. More data and parameters add little to extrapolation over syntax and semantics, so efficient architectures and training algorithms are needed.
record.recipe_differences: The paper benchmarks supervised sequence-to-sequence models on a handwritten arithmetic task; it does not reproduce the original loss-scaling method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling trends vary model size and training-set size; no comparison of fitting choices for pretraining-loss laws is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: For Transformer rel. uni. with symbol inputs, trained on HINT and evaluated on the LL subset, accuracy follows Y = 2.64 log M + 2.86 in model size and Y = 7.42 log D - 20.91 in data size (Fig. 3). Model size is up to about 35M parameters and data up to about 1M samples. Extrapolated, reaching 90% LL accuracy would need about 10^33 parameters and 10^15 examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On compositional arithmetic extrapolation (HINT), supervised Transformers' accuracy grows only log-linearly with model and data size, so scaling alone is impractical for high accuracy.

record.problems: The scaling evidence concerns accuracy on one task rather than pretraining loss. Figure 3 gives no uncertainty for the reported scaling equations; the text does not provide uncertainty or fitting details for those trends.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version results were reported. Other architecture and prompt comparisons concern HINT task accuracy rather than outcomes measured by V1–V7.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a power law in parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation of loss fits from small runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token split and its trend with compute.
Loss at fixed parameter count across depth/width; the architecture variants differ in mechanism, not shape at fixed size.
Power-law loss form in other modalities or regimes; only accuracy is fitted, with a log-linear form.
Downstream accuracy of pretrained language models as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of loss exponents or the compute-optimal split on setup or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: Rows r1 and r2 correctly carry versions ['none'] and state cannot_determine. The fits assume a log-linear trend, as the paper itself says ('Assuming a log-linear scaling trend'). No uncertainty or fitting details are given, and the scaled range is narrow: under one decade of model size. The Fig. 3 caption's 'training ... on the test subset LL' means evaluation on LL. The quoted 10^33 and 10^15 figures are consistent with base-10 logs in both equations. GPT-3 zero-shot and CoT results concern prompting, not scale, and bear on no version.
